findings.message: The CSV export still writes the Owner column as `p.ownerName ?? ""`. Every other owner display now goes through `ownerLabel` (118 AC-2), so the export can't tell an open proposal that needs an owner from a shipped one whose owner was never recorded. Fix: write `ownerLabel(p)` in that column, or note in the 118 change that exports leave ownerless rows blank on purpose.
findings.scenario: An open FLT-210 with no owner and a released FLT-188 with no owner → both have an empty Owner cell in proposals.csv, while the table shows 'Unassigned' and 'Not recorded'.

findings.message: Someone who doesn't manage credentials (an Engineer with git-accounts:read) now gets `unchecked` for a working app. The card shows a warning-tone 'Not checked' chip and puts 'only those who manage credentials can check the GitHub app' in the red `.err` style, so a healthy app looks broken to people who can't act on it. Keep the state honest but word it for that viewer: a neutral tone and a muted note instead of the error line. Also note who sees it in the 117 AC-3 records.
findings.scenario: Kasun (Engineer) opens /settings/integrations while the app is ready → a yellow 'Not checked' chip and a red error line, where before he saw 'Configured'.

findings.message: `github-app-states-117.test.ts` now keeps the `state` union in step with the module, but the rest of `GitHubAppStatus` (checkProblem, rotatedAt, callbackUrl, callbackProblem) is still a hand copy of what `githubAppStatus` returns. The page casts the tool result to it with `as GitHubAppStatus`, and nothing compares those fields. Extend the mirror test to check the returned keys, for example by calling the tool in an existing Postgres test and comparing its keys with the card type's.
findings.scenario: Renaming `checkProblem` in modules/git-accounts/server/read.ts → the card silently drops the reason line, and no test fails.
